title: Norm-rigidified Deuring gerbes and the two Picard actions
as_he_states: The proposed norm-rigidified categories should be μ_n-gerbes, and the two displayed Picard actions should agree; the comparison and the canonical norm object are explicitly left to be checked.
plausible_today: Specify a site, a central order of fixed degree, admissible invertible bimodules, norm lines, and their tensor compatibilities; prove local nonemptiness and a band-preserving equivalence with coherent compatibility of the two actions.
state_of_art: Assessment 19 November 2026. SGA4 XVIII §1.4.11–1.4.15 supplies the two-term Picard formalism; Voight (2021), §§18.3–18.4, supplies the maximal-order ideal model. Neither checked source proves every norm/action datum of the manuscript. C-SA06-700–701 separates the verified scalar μ_n band from this remaining comparison.
why_open: The page flags the action comparison. No opened historical source explains its abandonment; the explicit mathematical gap is local existence plus coherence, not the scalar-kernel calculation.
worth: Worth a focused reconstruction because the data are finite and explicit once the base and order are fixed.

title: The omitted norm-line obstruction at the ramification endpoint
as_he_states: The displayed sequence ends surjectively in the ramification quotient, with an uncertain homotopy-degree label.
plausible_today: For each ramification class retain the norm-line obstruction in Pic(A)/n; surjectivity is valid when this map vanishes, in particular in the principal bases used later.
state_of_art: Assessment 19 November 2026. The fppf Kummer sequence (Stacks, tag040N) and the central-ideal quotient in Voight §18.4 give the refined obstruction formulation proved in C-SA06-702. This run does not claim an explicit nonzero obstruction for every order.
why_open: The text supplies no reason for omitting the obstruction; the later principal-base calculations may explain why it becomes invisible, which is an inference here.
worth: Worth checking as a short prerequisite to any global norm-gerbe reconstruction.

title: A canonical norm object and lift of equivalences
as_he_states: Assume a canonical object T and seek lifts of ordinary equivalences to the norm-rigidified setting; the later canonical point is deleted and a residual sign remains.
plausible_today: Construct an equivalence torsor with its μ_2 automorphisms and describe any additional datum needed to choose a point; do not equate uniqueness of isomorphism classes with contractibility.
state_of_art: Assessment 19 November 2026. SGA4 XVIII Picard stacks and Deligne–Milne (1982), Theorem3.2, provide the categorical language; C-SA06-708–709 verifies that a neutral comparison need not neutralize either endpoint.
why_open: The deletion itself is evidence against an unconditional preferred point. No historical explanation beyond that correction was located.
worth: Worth resolving together with the action problem because it determines the precise canonicity one can claim.

title: The distinguished determinant orientation ξ_p
as_he_states: Determine ξ_p and prove the compatibility of the determinant of the rank-two slope-one-half crystal with the reduced-norm functor.
plausible_today: Fix covariant/contravariant Dieudonné convention, Frobenius and Verschiebung, the Tate determinant line, and a polarization; compute the resulting orientation modulo unit squares and verify its Morita transport.
state_of_art: Assessment 19 November 2026. Oda (1969), Corollary5.11 p131 and Propositions3.22–3.24 pp99–101, establish the degree-one comparison and polarization pairing. The exact integral orientation/Morita identity on these pages was not located. C-SA06-710 checks the matrix prerequisites only.
why_open: The source explicitly asks for ξ_p. No opened publication attributes a historical reason for leaving this particular normalization unresolved.
worth: High-value short project because it is concrete, testable and central to the proposed Deuring realization.

title: The real quaternionic realization and comparison neutrality
as_he_states: Construct the real quaternionic functor and compare its gerbe with the other realizations while retaining the nontrivial real obstruction.
plausible_today: Separate the Brauer class of a real quaternion algebra, its normed-line torsors and automorphisms; prove neutrality only for the comparison gerbe when an equivalence is actually supplied.
state_of_art: Assessment 19 November 2026. Deuring (1941) supplies the quaternionic algebra and Deligne–Milne (1982), §5, the real polarized Tannakian framework; C-SA06-709 gives the categorical distinction. None supplies the unnamed integral functor automatically.
why_open: The pages distinguish nonneutral real objects from a neutral comparison; treating these as a contradiction is an earlier-note error, not evidence that the construction was abandoned.
worth: Worth pursuing with the determinant problem because it checks the real place of the same proposed object.

title: Canonical finite fields and coherent Frobenius descent
as_he_states: Construct a canonical compatible finite-field system and deduce canonical equivalences after the displayed Frobenius quotient.
plausible_today: Use irreducible factors of cyclotomic polynomials with chosen compatible embeddings, then formulate the remaining choices as a groupoid and prove the required descent cocycle; quotient-level triviality alone is insufficient.
state_of_art: Assessment 19 November 2026. C-SA06-707 gives the exact counterexample F2[T]/Φ7≅F8×F8. C-SA06-705–706 verifies the class-level quotient calculation; the two-isomorphisms needed for coherent descent remain extra data. The searched gerbe sources do not match all these integral choices.
why_open: The manuscript retracts a canonical point; no later source found explains the fate of this exact finite-field presentation.
worth: Worth a tightly bounded coherence audit, with the false quotient formula removed before any further argument.

plausible_today: Use fppf μ_2-Kummer and the unit square classes 1,3,5,7 modulo8; the ramified ideal class still supplies a separate split factor of order2.

title: Maximal quadratic orders and twisting supersingular curves
as_he_states: The Frobenius relation F²+p=0 is used to pass to the ring of integers and to twist by invertible modules.

state_of_art: Assessment 19 November 2026. C-SA06-711 supplies E/F7:y²=x³+x with trace0 and only one rational nonzero2-torsion point, so (1+F)/2 is not an endomorphism. Deuring and Voight give the correct order classification.
why_open: The unqualified implication is false. There is no evidence in these pages that the author later imposed the missing endomorphism condition.
worth: Worth recording as a necessary repair before using the proposed twist classification.

title: The Brandt class sequence and its homotopy-fibre interpretation
as_he_states: Relate autoequivalences, strict generators, ideal classes, order types and local ramification, and interpret the resulting fibres.

why_open: The pages ask for interpretation rather than a missing numerical computation. A historical cause for nonpublication was not found.

title: Naturality of ideal representatives and Morita quasi-inverses
as_he_states: Choose a quasi-inverse from invertible bimodules to embedded ideals; the text explicitly warns that the choice is not natural.

worth: Worth documenting within the main Brandt reconstruction, not as a separate conjecture of canonical choice.

title: Condition(C) under localization, completion and base change
as_he_states: Commutativity of invertible two-sided ideals is used globally and questioned in local, completed and changed-base models.

why_open: No source records why the broad variants were left aside. The concrete obstacle is that a nonmaximal order may not retain the required commuting ideal model.
worth: Worth a finite local test-and-proof task for the exact orders used in the Deuring example.

as_he_states: A faithful commutative algebra with a positive adjoint should control the group, its norm character ε, the weight cocharacter and the distinguished complex cocharacters; several identifications are questioned.

title: Density and the disconnected rational-point trap
as_he_states: Use rational points and the compact kernel of ε to recover a torus and its real structure, with a disconnected example noted.
